summary: Port nails the 24 s four-regime cycle, its boundaries, scan speeds and every overlay pixel-for-pixel, but two of the four regimes are wrong in a major axis: the contour-band display loses its mirror symmetry (lower half of the panel goes black, 2 of 5 bands vanish) and the index-rainbow regime is ~4x too bright with a soft 44 px glow where the original draws a hard-edged 18 px window.
observations: Rig: grid, 256 px, 16x16 default. Neither side exposes any settable control (--probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for orig and port) — control surfaces match, dials: [].

Both sides run the SAME 24-second cycle of four 6-second regimes, and the regime boundaries land at identical times on both sides (t = 0/6/12/18 mod 24). Verified at 5 fps (survey), 20 fps (reg-* runs) and 40 fps (fps40 dump: both sides switch A->B at exactly t=6.000). No frame-rate coupling on either side. --skip 24 reproduces the --skip 0 stats on both sides (orig mean 8 / port mean 6), confirming the 24 s period.
Pattern is fully deterministic: seed 7 renders identical summary stats to seed 1 on both sides (orig mean 8 motion 3, port mean 6 motion 3). No RNG character to judge.

Both sides are resolution-adaptive: features scale with grid height (checked at 32x8 and 8x32 as well as the default 16x16). Regimes A, B and D are functions of the row only (all columns identical); regime C is driven by the flat pixel index (colour transitions occur mid-row and walk across row boundaries). Both sides agree on which regime uses which.

REGIME A (t 0-6 s), horizontal scan bar sweeping top->bottom once per window: POSITION AND SPEED MATCH EXACTLY. Brightness-weighted centroid of column 8 agrees to within 0.03 rows at all 20 dump times (e.g. t=2.75 both 7.00, t=3.95 both 10.00, t=5.15 both 13.00); ~2.67 rows/s, one wrap per 6 s on both sides.

REGIME A profile divergence: the original's bar is a soft 3-5 row footprint, the port's is a hard 1-2 rows. At pixel-aligned t=1.55 orig column reads [55,255,55], port [7,255,7] (shoulders 8x dimmer). At half-pixel t=0.95 orig reads [10,137,137,10], port [0,86,86,0] — port's peak is 37% lower and the 10-level outer shoulders are gone. Total column light: orig 294-365 across the sweep, port 172-269, i.e. the port carries 35-41% less light and flickers harder as the bar crosses pixel boundaries (min/max of total light 0.64 on port vs 0.81 on orig).

REGIME B (t 6-12 s) = a STATIC set of horizontal contour bands plus a vertical column sweeping left->right. ORIGINAL background is five evenly spaced bands, MIRROR-SYMMETRIC about the panel's horizontal centre line. On 16 rows: red 255 @row0, green 137 @row4 (10 @row3), dim red 55 @rows7-8, green 137 @row11 (10 @row12), red 254 @row15, everything else exactly 0. On 32 rows: red @0, green peak 193 @8, red 140 @rows15-16, green 193 @23, red 254 @31 — bands every 7.75 rows.

REGIME B port background is NOT symmetric and has only three features, all crowded at the edges. On 32 rows: red 255 @0 with a broad one-sided falloff 140/59/13 down rows 1-3, green peak 223 @8 with a wide skirt over rows 5-11, then rows 12-27 COMPLETELY BLACK, then 12/59/140/254 rising over rows 28-31. On 16 rows: 255 @0, 55 @1, green 191 @4 (91 @3, 28 @5), rows 6-13 all zero, 55 @14, 254 @15. The original's centre red band and its lower green band are missing entirely, so the bottom half of the panel is dead for 6 seconds out of every 24. Clearly visible side by side in reg-6/orig-motion.png vs reg-6/port-motion.png.

REGIME B sweeping column: speed and phase match (positions agree within 0.7 columns, usually under 0.2; ~2.5 cols/s, one full sweep per 6 s on both sides). Its colour profile inherits the same symmetry bug: orig's column runs red(edge)->green->red(centre)->green->red(edge) — R channel [163,87,35,6,0,18,58,122,122,58,18,6,0,35,87,163], symmetric with two cycles; the port's is a single monotonic yellow->green->red ramp — G channel [81,103,125,146,157,135,114,92,70,48,27,5,16,38,59,81], not symmetric. The port's column is also ~0.2 px broader (spills onto a second column at t=7.05 and t=8.05 where the original stays on one).
REGIME B base level: median max-channel over the whole frame is 10 on the original and 28 on the port (2.8x too bright).

REGIME C (t 12-18 s) = a hue ramp along the flat pixel index (~0.0245 hue/px, ~6.3 hue cycles over 256 px), drifting over time, plus a highlight window centred on the white cursor. Hue slope, cycle count, drift direction and drift rate all match between sides (measured from B/G channel ratios along row 0 at t=14: orig 0.10/0.10/0.20/0.30/0.40 at x=3/6/9/12/15, port 0.105/0.184/0.237/0.316/0.395).

REGIME C base brightness: original 10/255 (0.04), port 38/255 (0.15) — port is ~3.8x too bright. Median max-channel over the frame: orig 10, port 38, constant through the whole regime. Visually this is the difference between a near-black field with one bright bar (orig) and a full-frame rainbow wash (port) — see reg-12/orig.png vs reg-12/port.png. Summary stats for the t=12-18 window: orig meanBrightness avg 13.2 (min 9 max 26), port avg 26.8 (min 22 max 29).

REGIME C highlight shape: the ORIGINAL draws a HARD-EDGED rectangular run of exactly 18 pixels at a flat level 206 (flat indices 79-96 at t=14, centred on the white cursor at index 87), snapping straight back to the 10 base outside. The PORT draws a smooth bell ~40-44 px wide (indices ~68-107) climbing from 38 to a peak of 232 at index 86 and back down. So the port's highlight is ~2.4x wider with soft edges instead of a crisp window. The original's highlight level is a constant 206 all regime; the port's peak wobbles frame to frame (241/246/251).

REGIME D (t 18-24 s) = three static horizontal blocks: rows 0-3 black, 4-7 green, 8-11 yellow, 12-15 red (16-row grid). Structure is IDENTICAL on both sides. Only difference is level: orig 76, port 63 — port 17% dimmer, uniformly.

OVERLAYS present in all regimes match exactly. (1) A white cursor pixel walking the flat pixel index by +8 every 0.2 s: identical grid positions on both sides at every one of 21 sampled times ((2,0),(10,0),(3,1),(11,1),(4,2),(12,2),... ). (2) A red level indicator at pixel (15,15) cycling 50->255->51->152->153 every 0.2 s: byte-identical on both sides.

STATUS BLINK at pixel (0,0) is ~0.10 s EARLY on the port. Both sides run the same 1 s code (white held for ~4 frames, gap, a 0.15 s red flash, gap, a 0.15 s green flash, gap), but the original's red flash occupies frames t=18.95/19.00/19.05 while the port's occupies 18.85/18.90/18.95, and green orig 19.20-19.30 vs port 19.15-19.25. Consequence: at every exact integer second the original's corner pixel is red (255,0,0) and the port's is black — a visibly missing beat at 1 Hz.

Neither side reports a compile or runtime error; wantsSensors is false on both, so the beat120 feed is not involved. brightnessTrend is 'steady' on both sides in every regime window and zeroMotionFrames is 1 (the unavoidable first frame) over the 60 s survey — no dying/freezing port.
feedback: REGIME B (t 6-12 s of the 24 s cycle) is the biggest fix and the pattern's namesake display. The original's contour bands are mirror-symmetric about the panel's horizontal centre — the quantity being contoured is an ABSOLUTE / distance-from-centre value, not the raw vertical coordinate. Target on a 32-row grid: red band at row 0, green peak at row 8, red band straddling rows 15-16 (level 140 each), green peak at row 23, red band at row 31 — five bands at a 7.75-row pitch. The port currently produces red at row 0 (with a wrong broad 4-row falloff), green at row 8, rows 12-27 pure black, red at row 31. On the default 16x16 grid the target is red 255 @row0, green 137 @row4 (10 @row3), dim red 55 @rows7 AND 8, green 137 @row11 (10 @row12), red 254 @row15, all other rows exactly 0; the port currently gives 255/55/1/91/191/28 on rows 0-5 and nothing on rows 6-13.

REGIME B band SHARPNESS also differs: the original's bands are narrow (on 32 rows the top red band is 255,59,0,0 over rows 0-3 and the green band is 95,193,32 over rows 7-9), while the port's are broad (255,140,59,13 over rows 0-3 and 21,76,165,223,117,44,6 over rows 5-11). Tighten the contour falloff so a band occupies ~2-3 rows on a 32-row panel, not 7.

REGIME B and the whole background of REGIME C are far too bright on the port. Regime B's non-band base should be a median max-channel of ~10/255; the port sits at ~28/255. Regime C's rainbow base should be ~10/255; the port sits at ~38/255 (3.8x). The original reads as an almost-black field with one bright feature; the port reads as a lit rainbow wash. This one change alone would fix most of the visible difference in regime C.

REGIME C's highlight must be a HARD-EDGED window, not a soft glow: the original lights exactly 18 consecutive flat-index pixels at a flat level 206 (with the white cursor at the centre) and everything outside snaps to the 10 base. The port currently draws a smooth bell ~44 px wide peaking at 232. Replace the smooth falloff with a boolean/rectangular neighbourhood of ~18 px (~7% of the strip) at a constant level; also hold that level steady (orig is exactly 206 every frame, port's peak wobbles 241-251).

REGIME A: the scan bar's soft shoulders are missing. When the bar is pixel-aligned the original's column is [55,255,55]; the port's is [7,255,7]. When it sits between pixels the original is [10,137,137,10]; the port is [0,86,86,0]. Widen the bar's falloff so a pixel one row away from the centre keeps ~22% of the peak (55/255) and the half-offset peak reaches ~137, not 86. Position and speed are already exact — do not touch them.

REGIME D: uniform 17% brightness shortfall. The blocks should be at level 76 (green 0,76,0 / yellow 76,76,0 / red 76,0,0); the port renders 63. Everything else in that regime is byte-identical, so this is a single constant.

The corner status blink at pixel (0,0) fires ~0.10 s (2 frames at 20 fps) too early on the port: the original's red flash covers t=18.95-19.05 and green 19.20-19.30 within each 1 s beat, the port's are at 18.85-18.95 and 19.15-19.25. The flash durations (0.15 s) are already right; just delay the phase by ~0.1 s so the red flash straddles the integer second instead of preceding it.

Do NOT change: the 24 s cycle length, the four 6 s regime boundaries, the regime A row-scan speed (2.67 rows/s), the regime B column-sweep speed (2.5 cols/s), the regime C hue slope and drift, the regime D block layout, the white index cursor (+8 px every 0.2 s) or the (15,15) red level indicator — all of these already match the original exactly.
